review.summary:
Phase 21 is substantive, reproducible planning/provenance work, and — verified by reading bytes rather than prose — every one of the 11 findings from the rejected phase attempt-02 and all 9 remaining findings from both accepted chunk attempt-05 reviews is genuinely closed in current source cf84fe54. Because both chunk attempt-05 records are bound to bc704b5f (not the current hash), the PHASES.md:100-114 follow-up path applies and this review is the load-bearing coverage; I therefore checked each correction individually.

Phase attempt-02 mediums are closed by strengthening the gate, not softening a claim. `disposition()` (tools/red_team_management.py:216-266) now requires an exact reviewed SHA256 over every delta's path/kind/old/new identity *before* any classification (line 222), so whole added/removed subtrees carrying vendor defaults (`multi_turn_supported:false`, `type` const/default `client_session`) can no longer auto-classify; the three `startswith()` prefix matches are replaced by exact name sets (250-264), covered by test_whole_new_subtrees_and_unknown_prefixed_components_fail_closed. Renamed components are now content-bound: REVIEWED_SUCCESSORS (105-114) plus `verify_component_successor` (462-484) digest the whole successor object and assert each legacy `$ref` union prefix with a trailing-null-only exemption, with three regressions (successor_content_tampering, union_prefix_ignores_only_trailing_null, all_removed_components_have_real_successor). Stale registry entries now fail (556-561); `bindings()` raises on duplicate keys (355-357); `impl_contains` requires `pub` (337) and rejects `pub(crate)`/`pub(super)`; `deny.toml` is in the frozen-input list (check_phase.py:148) and asserted by test; PHASES.md:135 now names the dependency/advisory audit and the baseline-to-HEAD hygiene check with its network/full-history prerequisites at :228-231; the two imprecise assertions are fixed (test_management_phases.py:183-187, test_ci.py:496-501); the dead `phase == 21 or` disjunct is gone (test_ci.py:49); private_scan_history gives each of the eight superseded receipts a specific cause.

Chunk attempt-05 follow-ups are likewise closed: the plan now carries an explicit status-filter migration table and names FAILED/QUEUED/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/PARTIALLY_COMPLETE as no longer declared, with phase-22 rustdoc and phase-24 changelog deliverables (plan:152-168, 236-240); null stripping is trailing-only (473-474); baseline operations and per-row closures are precomputed once (562-564); the prompt template's glued digits are normalised (review_phase.py:521-522, 539) and the phase-status note is rewritten; docs/CI.md:149-152 states plainly that the ranged check is vacuous until the planning commit exists; PHASES.md:174-181 documents that an exhausted budget needs explicit maintainer authorization with no automatic reset, backed by test_exhausted_failure_has_no_automatic_budget_reset; manifest-reader discovery is now recursive over tools/ and scripts/ via os.walk.

Evidence is complete and current-source. docs/reviews/phase-21-attempt-03.checks.json records phase 21 at cf84fe54, source_unchanged true, passed true, no `scope` key (so check_evidence:210-217 would accept it and reject a contracts-only receipt); I reconstructed management_commands(21) by hand from check_phase.py:135-175 and its 25 entries match element for element and in order, every exit_code 0, timeout false. Captured output shows 34+23+51+35 = 143 green tests, verify-contracts --self-test rejecting 27 tampering cases including ten vendor-ownership cases, a real dependency audit (cargo-audit 0.22.2/cargo-deny 0.20.2 with pinned binary digests, RustSec 999ec89d freshHead, 1338 advisories, 206 packages, zero vulnerabilities, clean bans/licenses/sources), and a fresh private-material receipt at the same hash with zero identity/secret matches. I independently counted 160 `coverage` rows in contracts/airs-operations.json, 42 in the vendor operations ledger and 68 `category` rows in compatibility-decisions.json, matching the headline claims; manifest.json:1949-1963, 2032-2042 and 2442-2482 register the source, MIT license and four vendorArtifacts, and verify-contracts.py:29,393-407,471-489 keeps ownership narrowly scoped so the data-plane and Portkey corpora retain their own verifiers.

Residual issues are five lows, none blocking: `validate_review` is called without `phase` at review_phase.py:279 so the phase-21 >=9/10 floor is not re-applied in the second gate (reachable only by forging a self-inconsistent record under the declared trusted-writer model); the twice-requested proofreading fix still misses prose this scoped tool emits into its own artifacts and CLI, and the new research README; the shared enum decision string says "Extend declared values" on rows that are actually narrowings; `inventory['commit']` is never asserted equal to COMMIT; and the successor prefix guard only pins `$ref`/null branches present under matching keys. Categories 9.5/9/8.5/9.5/9.5 = 46/50 with every category >=8, no blocker/high/medium finding, and 9/10 clears the plan gate.

findings.description: verify_record applies the phase-aware gate twice with different inputs. Line 273-274 computes gate_decision(..., phase=phase) and requires record["decision"] to equal it, but the second call at line 279 invokes validate_review(...) without a phase argument (its signature at line 155 has no phase parameter), so the phase-21-only >=9/10 plan floor at line 70 is not re-applied there. A record that honestly states decision "rejected" (score 8.5, total 50, all categories 10) but whose gate_passed field is flipped to true therefore satisfies both gates: line 273-274 sees matching "rejected" values and line 276-281 sees gate_passed true plus validate_review returning True because its phase-blind gate_decision yields "accepted". main() never writes such a record (line 594 sets passed = passed and decision != "rejected"), and test_plan_score_floor_cannot_be_bypassed_by_category_total covers the realistic forgery where decision is also flipped, so nothing is wrong in this source state and PHASES.md:7 declares repository writers trusted. The gap is that this is precisely the mutual inconsistency the hashes and record checks exist to detect, and it sits on the one criterion this review is gated by.
findings.required_fix: Add a phase keyword to validate_review and pass phase=phase at tools/review_phase.py:279 (and at line 114 for consistency), or require record["gate_passed"] is True to imply the computed decision is not "rejected". Add a regression asserting that a record with decision "rejected" and gate_passed true fails verify_record for phase 21.

findings.description: The glued-digit proofreading fix requested by phase attempt-02 finding 7 and governance chunk attempt-05 finding 1 was applied to the five scoped documents and to the review_phase.py prompt template, but the identical defect remains in prose this scoped tool emits. Line 592 writes 'phase23 must exercise old consumers and round-trips' into contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json:27162-area, line 525 writes 'phase22 implements overlay' into contracts/airs-active-sources.json:76, line 611 is the maintainer-facing CLI error 'Phase22-25 implementation/qualification evidence is not implemented', and lines 423 and 606 put 'Phase21-only'/'Phase21 only:' into the docstring and --help text. The newly added audit document docs/research/2026-10-19-prisma-airs-openapi/README.md is pervasively affected (:263 'all42operation mappings and the9functional dependency closures plus33error-metadata closures', :342 'capped2MiB each, context100MiB', :506 'all64 object-component classifications and320 property comparisons'), and the immutable seed carries 'phase21 baseline diff' at contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json:27248. These are the documents a future maintainer reads to re-derive the pins, and the fix was requested twice.
findings.required_fix: Normalise spacing before numerals in the emitted strings at tools/red_team_management.py:423, 525, 592, 606, 611 and in docs/research/2026-10-19-prisma-airs-openapi/README.md and REVIEW.md; update RETENTION_SHA256 if the seed's sourceLedgerEvidence sentence is corrected, and regenerate the affected contract artifacts with tools/red_team_management.py so --check stays byte-exact.

findings.description: The single most user-visible delta is the TargetStatusFilter enum narrowing from seven declared values to exactly DRAFT and ACTIVE (:2858-2884, old/new recorded losslessly). Its machine-readable decision string, shared by the enum group at tools/red_team_management.py:260-261, reads 'Extend declared values; retain old response values and legacy status inputs; do not invent filter mappings.' The first clause describes an extension and is wrong for this row and for the ProfilingStatus INIT/QUEUED removal that reuses the same text; only the trailing clauses apply. The category (compatibility_exception) and the plan prose (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:152-168) are both correct, so no decision is actually mistaken, but compatibility-decisions.json is the artifact phases 22-25 and the phase-25 drift detector consume, and its narrative for the headline narrowing mis-describes the change.
findings.required_fix: Split the enum-group decision in tools/red_team_management.py:260-261 so narrowing/removal rows carry text naming the removed values and the migration (or add a per-row 'direction' field), regenerate the artifact, and assert in tools/test_red_team_management.py that the TargetStatusFilter enum row's decision text names the narrowed domain.

findings.description: build() loads the hash-pinned audit inventory and checks that its spec paths equal COUNTS and that the management row exists, but never compares inventory['commit'] (docs/research/2026-10-19-prisma-airs-openapi/inventory.json:2) with the module COMMIT constant at line 25. COMMIT is then stamped into every output as observedCommit and snapshotCommit (lines 516, 595-596) and into SOURCE_ID. Provenance correctness therefore rests on two independently maintained constants happening to agree rather than on one asserted equality. The practical exposure is narrow: for the management source a mismatch would fail checked_bytes, but the six already-adopted sources have activeSpecificationSha256 equal to frozenSha256, so re-pinning inventory.json to a different upstream commit whose bytes are unchanged would silently relabel their observedCommit. Separately, the management row's own activeSpecificationPath/activeSpecificationSha256 fields in inventory.json still point at the frozen baseline and are ignored by the tool, which is harmless but inconsistent with the artifact the tool emits.
findings.required_fix: Assert inventory['commit'] == COMMIT immediately after loading the inventory in build(), and add a test patching the inventory commit that expects an explicit provenance error.

findings.description: verify_component_successor.prefixes() now correctly strips only a trailing {'type': 'null'} branch, closing the attempt-05 finding, but the comparison it performs is narrower than the invariant the plan states at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:289-290 ('verify each old union reference prefix'). It enforces left == right only when the legacy branch is a $ref or the null literal (line 478); an inline structural legacy branch at the same index may be replaced or altered without tripping the guard, and the loop iterates old.keys() & new.keys(), so a successor that renamed a union key (for example multi_turn_config's oneOf to anyOf) is skipped entirely. The current eight renames all use $ref branches, so the guard is fully effective on this diff, and the successor content digest in REVIEWED_SUCCESSORS still forces re-review of any such change. This is precision rather than an active hole, but phase 25 inherits this comparator for drift classification.
findings.required_fix: Compare branch lists by index for all branch shapes (not only $ref/null), and raise when a successor drops or renames a union key present in the removed variant; add regressions covering an altered inline legacy branch and a oneOf-to-anyOf rename.

evidence: Check evidence is complete, genuinely executed and current-source: docs/reviews/phase-21-attempt-03.checks.json:2-6 records phase 21, source_sha256 cf84fe545acaee705eef797f3961cf40526f2cd384fd9c057eac7fae0c68e1ec (the reviewed hash), source_unchanged true, checked_at 2026-10-19T14:02:50.366779+00:00, passed true and no 'scope' key, so review_phase.check_evidence:210-217 would accept it and would reject the contracts-only receipt. I reconstructed management_commands(21) by hand from tools/check_phase.py:135-175 (frozen-baseline diff with the planning-fixture exclusion, verify_planning_fixture+verify_planning_gateway_proof, the untracked-SDK-file assertion, the baseline..HEAD ranged hygiene diff with all three vendor YAML exclusions, the 10-command common block in order ending in check-private-material, then check-dependencies, test_ci, model_fixtures/generate_constants/response_defaults, verify_native_fixtures --require-test-bindings, red_team_dataplane --check --require-complete, schema-oracle.mts, verify-gateway-specimens.mts, generate_validation, generate_models) and it matches the 25 recorded entries element for element and in order; every entry has a resolved invocation array, exit_code 0 and timeout false. docs/checks/phase-21.json:2-6 carries the identical phase, hash, timestamp and passed flag.

Every phase attempt-02 finding is closed in current source, each verified by reading the repair: disposition() requires REVIEWED_DELTAS[tuple(path)] to equal sha256(encoded(identity)) for every delta before classification (tools/red_team_management.py:220-223), so whole-subtree additions can no longer bypass review, and the three startswith() matches are now exact name sets (250-264) with test_whole_new_subtrees_and_unknown_prefixed_components_fail_closed covering RestConnectionParamsFuture and an added default-bearing property; REVIEWED_SUCCESSORS (105-114) plus verify_component_successor (462-484) bind each renamed component's successor content to a digest and assert legacy union prefixes, with test_successor_content_tampering_rejected exercising drop/required/reorder and test_union_prefix_ignores_only_trailing_null exercising a relocated null branch; bindings() raises on duplicates via add() (355-357, test_duplicate_audit_operation_rejected); impl_contains requires 'pub' (337) with test_private_and_crate_visible_functions_are_not_public_bindings covering '', 'pub(crate) ' and 'pub(super) '; deny.toml is in the phase-21 frozen paths (check_phase.py:148) and asserted at test_management_phases.py:24; docs/PHASES.md:135 names the dependency/advisory audit and the baseline-to-HEAD hygiene check and :228-231 records the network/full-history prerequisites; test_management_phases.py:183-187 uses argument-level substring checks; test_ci.py:496-501 asserts bootstrap_reference.py precedes the gate whenever a selected command resolves under node_modules; test_ci.py:49-53 derives fetch-depth purely from range presence; docs/phase-status.json:5374-5427 gives each superseded private-scan receipt its own specific cause.

Both accepted chunk attempt-05 records sit at source bc704b5f8a8dae6f358a32391765e462af5ca9c0d7dab44f4c7b24436e450b24, not the current hash, so accepted_chunks (review_phase.py:355-366) routes through the attempt-5 follow-up path and requires this accepted current-source phase review; I verified all nine of their remaining findings are closed. Plan-and-provenance: the status-filter migration is now an explicit deliverable (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:152-168 table plus 'Phase 22 must add rustdoc on TargetListOptions::status and profiling_status; Phase 24 must repeat the migration guidance in the changelog' and :236-240); null stripping is trailing-only (473-474); unused REVIEWED_DELTAS/REVIEWED_SUCCESSORS entries now fail (556-561, test_stale_review_registry_entries_are_rejected); baseline_operations and baseline_closures are precomputed once before the delta loop (562-564). Governance: review_phase.py:521-522 and :539 read 'strictly above 40' and 'remains 46/50', :406 and :542 read 'Phase 20'/'phase 20', check_phase.py:185 reads 'phase 24 milestone gate'; the phase-21 note at docs/phase-status.json:5184-5185 is rewritten with normal spacing; docs/CI.md:149-152 states the ranged check is vacuous before the planning commit and that the worktree/index diffs carry the coverage; docs/PHASES.md:174-181 documents the maintainer-authorization remedy with no automatic reset, asserted by test_exhausted_failure_has_no_automatic_budget_reset; test_every_manifest_reader_is_selected_or_explicitly_explained now walks tools/ and scripts/ recursively via os.walk with node_modules/__pycache__/test_* excluded and four reviewed nonempty exemptions.

Artifact counts are independently reproducible from the committed bytes rather than taken on trust: I counted 160 'coverage' rows in contracts/airs-operations.json, 42 in contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/operations.json and 68 'category' rows in compatibility-decisions.json, matching the tool's printed 'AIRS contracts: 7 source pins, 160 operation mappings, 42 management operations; static evidence only' and REVIEWED_DELTAS' 68 registered paths exactly (the unused-identity check at 556-561 makes the two sets equal by construction). contracts/airs-active-sources.json lists all seven sources with operationCounts 18/23/47/42/5/21/4 = 160, the management row alone marked adoptionState pinned_for_phase22_not_runtime_adopted with frozenSha256 4b92495d differing from activeSpecificationSha256 5fbb533b, and the data-plane row using identityKind source_metadata against a hashed source.json. Every operation row carries the honest label 'native_method_exists; static_mapping_only; not_live_acceptance'.

Vendor ownership is narrowly and completely scoped: tools/verify-contracts.py:29 sets VENDOR_ROOTS to only contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0, :471-478 sweeps the product parent and rejects any file outside a registered version, :479-489 requires exact equality between the manifested corpus set and the on-disk set, and :393-407 requires each vendorArtifact to live under a registered root, be hash-tracked, have a redistributed source inside those roots, and match that source's repository/commit/license and the license record's origin. The recorded --self-test run rejected 27 tampering cases including unowned-vendor-file, missing-vendor-file, modified-vendor-file, vendor-license-commit, duplicate-source-id, vendor-artifact-origin, vendor-artifact-omission, vendor-artifact-escape, vendor-symlink and unowned-vendor-version. contracts/manifest.json:1949-1963 registers the source, :2032-2042 the MIT license at commit 582e30543bf2, and :2442-2482 the four vendorArtifacts; the data-plane and Portkey trees are absent from corpus_roots and keep their dedicated verifiers, exactly as the plan requires. verify_management_metadata (431-448) checks all 21 source.json fields against the manifest entry, the parsed spec, the actual YAML bytes, the git blob SHA1 and the license bytes, with test_source_metadata_every_field_is_verified damaging each field in turn.

The SDK freeze holds with a byte-exact metadata exception: the recorded git diff --exit-code against 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e over crates/scm-sdk, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE, deny.toml and the six frozen ledgers exits 0, and git ls-files --others over the same paths confirms no untracked SDK file. require_only_hash_replacements (check_phase.py:79-91) admits only 64-hex values occurring exactly once as quoted tokens and then demands full byte equality; verify_planning_fixture (93-120) applies it to model-regressions.json and the oracle corpus, resolves the corpus path from the baseline object so 'source' cannot be redirected, rejects symlinks and requires the rebound manifest hash to equal current contracts/manifest.json bytes; verify_planning_gateway_proof (123-132) allows exactly two input hashes and fails closed if the allowlist is incomplete. test_only_fixture_source_hash_can_be_rebound, test_provenance_guard_rejects_reformatting_and_other_bytes and test_gateway_proof_allows_only_two_rebound_input_hashes prove reindentation, trailing newlines, value changes, input reordering and a third rebound hash all raise.

Retention is floor-bound, additive-only and origin-verified: retained_floor (391-419) reads the floor only from the hash-pinned immutable seed (RETENTION_SHA256 25a77256..., RETENTION_COMMIT 0a213fe7, sdkVersion 0.2.2), rejects duplicate baselineIds, indexes exports/methods/redTeamExtraMethods by identity so the check stays linear, compares Portkey rows on (method, path, operationId, rustMethod, operationName) only, and emits {**current, floorReference, preservationCheck} rather than copying the seed - contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json:23501-23505 carries floorReference with no sourceLedgerSha256/auditedSourceCommit/sdkVersion. verify_retention_origin (422-429) rehashes all six RETENTION_LEDGER_PATHS against seed digests (contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json:27249-27256) and ran under the phase-21-only flag. The suite proves removal from each of nine sections, an emptied rustPaths list, a changed default, a one-byte seed change and a wrong recorded digest all raise, while additions pass and still point at the seed hash.

Security posture is clean and the planning boundary is honest. docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json is bound to the same cf84fe54 source with passed true, 1916 git-visible files, zero selected identity/secret matches, zero published-source registration matches and three unchanged preexisting tenant occurrences with newOrChangedFilesCount 0; the gate's recorded invocation returned receiptFresh true / privateScanReexecuted false, which the receipt itself discloses as a limitation. safe_path (141-153) rejects absolute paths, '..' components, symlinks at any level and any resolution outside ROOT; load() refuses any unpinned file in the audit directory; closure() raises on external references; read_yaml (red_team_dataplane.py:59-61) passes the path as argv with no shell and asserts js-yaml 4.3.2 before parsing. The CI contracts job pins every action by commit SHA, sets permissions contents:read, persist-credentials:false and fetch-depth:0 (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:8-26), and check_phase.main:691-694 stamps the contracts scope marker into a separate phase-21-contracts.json receipt so the subset can never qualify a review even though it currently equals the full 25 commands.

Later-phase scope fails closed and the governance gates are real: red_team_management.py:610-611 raises unconditionally for --require-through-phase above 21 with test_future_phase_cannot_pass_on_plan_artifacts executing the CLI for 22-25 and asserting nonzero exit plus the explicit message; management_commands drops the 0.2.2-specific release helper (check_phase.py:186) and rewrites inherited phase-19/20 receipt paths, with test_future_milestones_require_explicit_complete_artifacts asserting no argument contains '0.2.2' or a phase-19/20 receipt path; phase 21 deliberately omits native_exports/live_evidence per the documented evidence-scope boundary at docs/PHASES.md:204-212 and test_plan_retains_static_closure_without_claiming_current_live_proof asserts both return for phases 23 and 24. gate_decision:69-86 rejects on any blocker/high before scoring, targets 42 for chunks and 46 for phases, grants accepted_with_deficiencies only at attempt 5 with exactly four completed priors, and line 70 independently rejects any phase-21 phase-level review below 9/10; declared_chunk_scope:221-249 enforces ordered immutable scope_revisions whose last entry equals the current scope and resolves the revision in force at each historical attempt; verify_attempt_sequence:89-132 re-reads every prior record with is_file()/is_symlink() guards, re-validates its review, compares its CLI envelope and requires the exact 'Chunk scope artifacts: [...]' line in its preserved prompt.

The plan's design decisions are grounded in the actual vendor bytes and are internally consistent. docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md settles the union/discriminator policy (legacy first-success order preserved when 'type' is absent, new client_session branch requiring an explicit literal tag and never inserting its vendor default), the five per-operation target response declarations with their credential/redaction properties, the six explicit endpoint profiles with unchanged api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com defaults and no automatic following of the advertised api.sase host, the retention ordering decision separating identity-set inventories from the runtime union-branch contract guarded by contracts/native-union-variants.json, and the exact reviewed-delta digest procedure that the tool's docstring (lines 7-11) and its rejection diagnostic (line 223) reproduce verbatim so a reviewer can act on a failure. disposition() raises on any path containing 'required', on a property literally named description/title/example (line 230), on removals outside the eight known renames, on non-schema deltas including any new route, and on target-parameter changes other than the single profiling_status filter whose anyOf[ProfilingStatusFilter,null] shape and required:false it checks explicitly (234-246); test_structural_annotation_names_removals_and_security_fail_closed, test_parameter_list_removal_cannot_masquerade_as_filter_addition, test_semantic_type_and_enum_narrowing_fail_closed and test_added_and_changed_constraints_require_exact_review execute those paths.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep with no shell: I could not recompute the reviewed source fingerprint cf84fe54..., the checks snapshot hash 3b334c16..., or any file sha256, and I could not re-execute any of the 25 checks or the four test suites. I verified evidence by reading the recorded invocations, exit codes and captured output, by reconstructing management_commands(21) by hand and comparing it element for element and in order, and by independently cross-reading the artifacts those commands assert over (including direct counts of 160/42/68 rows).

Static evidence only, as the artifacts themselves state. Native-binding verification proves a named public inherent method exists; it does not prove request construction, generated Rust correctness, wire acceptance or tenant permissions. The five response-declaration fixtures, both response modes, typed round-trips, old-consumer source compatibility, MSRV/current-compiler regressions and live acceptance belong to phases 22-24 and were not judged; I did not treat later-phase operations marked planned as missing phase-21 deliverables.

The baseline-to-HEAD committed hygiene check named in docs/PHASES.md:135 is currently vacuous: docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json:5 records headCommit 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e, equal to MANAGEMENT_BASELINE, so the recorded exit 0 for that command proves nothing about this phase's content. Actual whitespace coverage comes from the unranged worktree and index diffs, which do cover the staged additions. docs/CI.md:149-152 states this honestly, which is the remedy the governance chunk review requested, so I record it as a limitation of the evidence rather than a defect.

No remote CI run of the re-pointed phase-21 workflow exists. Phase-21 CI coverage is committed configuration plus local guard evidence; docs/CI.md:167-169 and docs/RELEASE.md:9-13 state this honestly and I did not treat a terminal remote run as a phase-21 requirement. I did not re-audit historical release infrastructure or reopen phases 1-20.

docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json are excluded from the review fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:15-16), so record, prompt, CLI-envelope and snapshot integrity rests on self-reported hashes inside those same unfingerprinted files, and chunk scope declarations are not source-hash bound. A consistently edited set would be undetectable from inside this review. This is pre-existing design, not a phase-21 regression. The snapshot git status also shows docs/checks/phase-21.json and docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json with differing index and working tree; both are fingerprint-excluded and I read only the working-tree copies.

The upstream byte observations in docs/research/2026-10-19-prisma-airs-openapi/inventory.json are a committed, hash-pinned snapshot of a prior network audit. I verified that the vendored and frozen files match those recorded hashes but could not and did not re-fetch pan.dev commit 582e30543bf2 to confirm the snapshot itself, which is also why I record the missing inventory['commit'] == COMMIT assertion as a finding. I performed no network calls and modified no files.

My conclusion that the classifier's remaining precision gaps (successor prefix comparison, union key renames) are not exercised by the current diff rests on reading the eight recorded rename deltas and their successors rather than executing verify_component_successor; the supporting regressions are recorded as passing but I could not run them.

I did not read any credential or tenant-registration material and did not leave the repository. .local/typescript appears only as the recorded --baseline argument of verify-contracts.py and the recorded tsx path for schema-oracle.mts; I did not inspect it.
